useCase.name: Handle a student who misses a quiz without recording a false zero

intent.name: quiz.makeup.offer
intent.summary: Decide to give a student who missed a quiz a second go, and say how. One step, and no approval stands in the way.

routesElsewhere.note: A makeup is offered against an absence that is already recorded (E5).
Offering records the decision and the route. Reopening the window for that student is the act itself (BR-5).
The teacher decides whether to offer a makeup. Because a quiz is informal this needs neither coordinator approval nor admin release, and requiring one would mean quizzes are never put right (BR-4).
Where no makeup is offered the quiz stays out of the average and the absence stands. Nothing is counted as zero by default (BR-7).

steps.note: One step. The teacher decides, and no approval or release stands between the decision and the record (BR-4, BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A student not marked absent arrives as an error — there is no absence for a makeup to answer.
plan.atomicity: One write: the decision, its route and the audit entry together or not at all. Where a makeup is offered the quiz stays out of the average until the score is recorded; where none is offered the absence stands and the quiz stays out of the average for good (BR-7). Nothing is counted as zero either way (BR-2).

Reopening was chosen for a quiz held on paper.
errors.note: A paper quiz carries no window (UC-06-08 BR-6). It is given printed and marked by hand.

planningRules.rule: Never decide whether a makeup is offered. It is the teacher's own decision (BR-4), and the reason it needs no approval is the same reason a planner must not make it for them.
Never choose the route. Reopening the online quiz and handing over a printed one are different arrangements with the student (BR-5).
Never record a zero where no makeup is offered. The quiz stays out of the average and the absence stands — nothing is counted as zero by default (BR-7, BR-2).
Never route this through an approval. A quiz absence needs no classification, no approval and no release (BR-11), and inserting one is how quizzes stop being put right at all.
Never plan the reopening in the same step. Offering records the decision; reopening the window for that student is the separate act that lets them sit it (BR-5).

reversal.statement: A decision is recorded again rather than withdrawn. Where a makeup was offered and is not taken, the student is absent again and the quiz stays out of the average (BR-10).

intent.name: quiz.makeup.score.record
intent.summary: Record the score a student earned in a quiz makeup, tagged as a makeup, replacing the absence. One step.

hath se check kar liya, 15 number hain
routesHere.gloss: marked it by hand, it is 15

routesHere.gloss: record the score for the quiz they took again

routesElsewhere.note: A student absent from the makeup too is recorded absent again, and the quiz stays out of the average (BR-10).

request.text: ye number imtihan ke natije mein daal do
request.gloss: put this mark into the exam result

routesElsewhere.note: None of this touches the formal examination flow (BR-11), and a quiz result does not enter the formal examination result (UC-06-08 BR-10).

steps.note: One step. The makeup score replaces the Absent flag and is tagged as a makeup, so a mark earned in a second sitting is distinguishable (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A score above the quiz total, and a score for a student who was not marked absent, arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the score, the makeup tag, the cleared Absent flag and the recalculated average together or not at all. The quiz re-enters the student's average from that moment, and the family is told the result (BR-9). Where the quiz had already been closed and averaged, the average recalculates when the score is recorded (E6).

planningRules.rule: Never supply the score. It goes to the family as their child's result (BR-9), and a figure a planner produced is a mark nobody awarded.
Say that the quiz re-enters the average. It was out of it while the absence stood (BR-2); recording the score changes the student's average, which is what the family sees next.
Never present the mark as a formal exam mark. None of this touches the formal examination flow (BR-11).
Never record a makeup score where no absence stands. There is nothing to replace, and an ordinary mark upload is the right route (E5).

reversal.statement: A score is corrected by recording it again while the quiz is open to correction. The absence it replaced stays on the record as what happened first.
